accepted_facts: In a synthetic 4-node model with a single common skewed driver spread through a shared lag-1..3 HRF-like kernel (no instantaneous three-way term by construction), static co-skewness alone predicts the cognition target: CV-R2 0.478 (std 0.046, 12 seeds).
Its incremental CV-R2 over a directed / multi-lag FC baseline collapses to ~0: -0.0007 (std 0.0018) over a few-lag directed baseline and -0.0011 over a 6-lag VAR-style baseline.
Over a static LINEAR FC baseline co-skewness keeps only a small increment (0.0265, std 0.0125), which the directed baseline then absorbs.
Without a common driver (independent-source control) co-skewness carries no prediction (-0.031, std 0.016), so the effect requires a shared skewed source.
rejected_or_quarantined_evidence: Several CON counterexamples were invalid or irrelevant: a model with no predictive co-skewness, a non-stationary VAR that overflowed, and a phase-randomization script that crashed.

The residual increment of co-skewness over a richer directed baseline on real data: reported small but run-to-run unstable in the transcript; quarantined as unresolved rather than treated as evidence either way.
argument_quality: PRO held the original falsifier frame, iteratively repaired weak points in the generative model, and clearly separated the synthetic sufficiency demonstration from the real-data test the thesis actually needs. CON sharpened at the end (correctly flagging the instability of the last multi-lag result and proposing reasonable quantitative thresholds for a future HCP test), but within the transcript this refined the remaining uncertainty rather than refuting PRO.
protocol_conduct: Decisive test pre-registered before compute and schema-valid; real compute with 12 fixed deterministic seeds; order-swap audit PASS (substantive call 'unclear' on both the natural and swapped runs); a verbosity-confound warning is flagged because CON was substantially longer than PRO.
evidence_quality: Real, deterministic, rerunnable compute, but on a SYNTHETIC generative model rather than real fMRI/BOLD. The decisive observable is a proxy (not paper-faithful) and establishes SUFFICIENCY of the leakage mechanism, not its necessity in real data. Bounded by 4 nodes, one common driver, one symmetric nuisance, a shared fixed HRF kernel and Ridge alpha fixed at 1.0.

what_it_supports.statement: That a lagged, shared, skewed driver is SUFFICIENT to make static co-skewness predict cognition while a directed lagged-FC baseline absorbs almost all of that predictive power (increment ~0.00).
That the effect requires a common skewed source: it vanishes in the no-common-driver control.
That, in this regime, co-skewness behaves as a static proxy for unmodelled directed/temporal structure rather than as an irreducible instantaneous three-way interaction.

what_it_does_not_support.statement: That real BOLD co-skewness IS this identifiability artifact: synthetic sufficiency does not establish that real fMRI lives in this regime.
Any discovery-level or data-level claim about the seed paper's empirics.
That co-skewness carries no genuine higher-order signal in general — only that an artifactual route is sufficient to reproduce the reported predictive power here.

what_remains_open: Whether static co-skewness retains a substantial, stable incremental CV-R2 over a properly matched directed/VAR baseline on the same subjects (e.g. HCP).
Whether co-skewness prediction survives a temporal/phase shuffle that preserves instantaneous marginals on real data.
Whether richer real covariance structure (more nodes, region-specific HRFs) leaves a residual increment a directed baseline does not absorb.
permitted_wording: On a synthetic model, a lagged common skewed driver was sufficient to make static co-skewness predict cognition while a directed lagged-FC baseline absorbed almost all of it (increment ~0.00).
The duel showed the leakage mechanism is a plausible, sufficient explanation; it did not show that real BOLD co-skewness is this artifact.
PRO prevailed on argumentation; the substantive merits-call on the claim remains unclear pending a real-data test.
forbidden_wording: Proven / demonstrated that co-skewness is just an artifact (the test is synthetic sufficiency, not real-data necessity).
Shown on fMRI / HCP data (no real data was used).
The seed paper's finding is refuted / co-skewness carries no real higher-order signal.
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate confidence within a narrow scope: on the synthetic model the pre-registered sufficiency signature is cleanly realized (co-skewness predictive alone, ~0 increment over directed FC, absent without a common driver), and the order-swap audit is stable with a substantive call of 'unclear' on both runs. Out of scope: no real fMRI/BOLD test, no real directed/VAR baseline, no temporal-shuffle control on data; the decisive observable is a proxy, not paper-faithful. Genre: scout — a synthetic sufficiency probe, not a scientific_result.
